question: What was the revised International Poverty Line (IPL) set by the World Bank for India in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**$3.00/day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **June 2025**, the **World Bank** officially updated the **International Poverty Line (IPL)** to **$3.00 per day**, a significant increase from the previous standard of **$2.15 per day** established in **2022**.
 
• This revision is based on the latest **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** data, which accounts for changes in the global **cost of living** and **inflation** rates across different nations.
 
• For **India**, this update is particularly relevant as it serves as a benchmark for international organizations to assess the progress of **poverty alleviation** programs and economic growth.
 
• The **$3.00/day** threshold is used to define **extreme poverty** globally, ensuring that the metric reflects the minimum cost for basic food, clothing, and shelter in the current economic climate of **2025**.
